title: Playing the Show Ball and with pianist Bob Dougherty
summary: Sal recalls playing with Bob Dougherty and his wife Pauline, and meeting a friend's son.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: I want to go out. I want to go out. I want to go out. I was playing the train lead, you know. I was talking, bing bop, bing on that jazz, you know. That's the kind of show that was. At the show ball? Yeah. You played at the show ball? Yeah, I played at Confucian Ice there. I could tell you the bad part. I played one night at the Pete Herman's. They were made so mad, man. Some Mexican things, they were good, you know. I might criticize, they were good. They were good. But they were knocking me, man. That made me mad. I was playing the show cold taking.

I was playing the show cold taking. And that woman said, Who's the drummer in there? I said, me. Anything wrong? I was playing with Bob Doher, man. You said, Bob Doher, you met Bob? Mm-hmm. He was a fine piano player, Bob. Bob and I used to go out between the sets to go get a little snort, you know. There you go. Great show. I said, Bob, two weeks ago, went to his house, man. And Pauline put in the bed. And Bob says, man, Pauline, you got a hard ball. I said, bring the hard ball, Pauline. I said, more down, sweetheart. I said, go on, still more beer, man. She said, let's go home. This one.
Another lawyer can of his wife, huh? Yes, Bob. Pauline.

Pauline. I said, West Wiles from that neighborhood, man. Albert Oman around that neighborhood, man. Married his wife there. Oman's an old schoolboy there, man. And Steve's son is Steve Lloyd from California. Man, that guy jumped up and hugged me, man. When I had the hurricane, Betsy, he made a speech at the other state with Steve Lloyd. I said, Steve Lloyd, you know what? Hello, son. Glad to see you. Right? And then he said, you married this guy? He's great. But she don't think so.
